input.strategy_title: Idle resource reporting in the web console
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Cluster administrators cannot see which resources are sitting idle: workbenches
nobody has touched in weeks keep their volumes and reservations, and old
pipeline runs accumulate storage. Admins ask for a single report in the RHOAI
web console showing idle and stale resources per project so they can reclaim
capacity with confidence. The notebook controller already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata — the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Administrators can export either report as CSV. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. |

## Affected Components

- RHOAI web console
- Notebook controller
- Kubeflow Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources
- Cost/chargeback calculations

## Open Questions

None.

# Idle and stale resource reports in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers administrator-facing idle and stale resource reporting in
the RHOAI web console. Cluster administrators get a per-project view of idle
workbenches (with last activity, owner, and reserved resources) and stale
pipeline runs (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained
artifacts), plus CSV export of either report. The data is sourced from
capabilities that already exist in the platform — the notebook controller's
last-activity tracking and Kubeflow Pipelines run completion metadata — so all
code changes land in the web console; no changes are made to the notebook
controller or the pipelines component.

## Scope

- A per-project idle-workbench report in the web console showing, for each
  workbench: last activity (sourced from the notebook controller's activity
  tracking), owner, and reserved resources.
- A stale pipeline-run report in the web console showing completed runs older
  than a configurable age, with their retained artifacts, sourced from
  Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- A configurable staleness age threshold for the pipeline-run report.
- CSV export of either report, containing the same columns as the on-screen
  report.
- Validation that reported values reconcile with the upstream data sources
  (notebook controller activity tracking and Kubeflow Pipelines run
  metadata) — these components keep working unchanged; correctness of the
  reports against them is part of this epic's deliverable.
- Read-only reporting only. Automated reclamation or deletion of idle
  resources and cost/chargeback calculations are out of scope and must not be
  introduced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches with differing last-activity times,
  the console renders a per-project idle-workbench report listing each
  workbench's last activity, owner, and reserved resources.
- The idle-workbench report's last-activity values reconcile with the
  notebook controller's activity tracking for the same workbenches
  (spot-checked against the source data).
- Given completed pipeline runs of varying age, the stale pipeline-run report
  lists exactly the completed runs older than the configured age, together
  with their retained artifacts, and its values reconcile with Kubeflow
  Pipelines run completion metadata.
- The staleness age threshold is configurable, and changing it changes which
  runs appear in the stale pipeline-run report.
- Either report can be exported as CSV, and the exported file contains the
  same rows and columns as the on-screen report and opens correctly in
  standard spreadsheet tools.
- The reports expose no reclamation, deletion, or cost-calculation actions
  (read-only; out-of-scope guard).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)** — Primary. The per-project idle-workbench report (last
  activity, owner, reserved resources) sourced from the notebook controller's
  activity tracking.
- **HLR-2 (P1)** — Primary. The stale pipeline-run report (completed runs
  older than a configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from
  Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- **HLR-3 (P2)** — Bundled. CSV export of either report shares the same
  reporting UI surface, data structures, and query paths as the P1 reports;
  it is not separately schedulable and is delivered inside this epic.

# Documentation for idle and stale resource reports

## Description

This epic delivers Red Hat documentation explaining the idle-workbench and
stale pipeline-run reports in the RHOAI web console: what each report shows,
where the data comes from, how to configure the staleness age threshold, how
to export a report as CSV, and the steps administrators should follow to
safely reclaim capacity based on the reports. The documentation is written
after the reporting capability is implemented so it describes what actually
shipped.

## Scope

Content outline for the documentation set:

- Overview of the idle and stale resource reporting feature: the problem it
  solves for cluster administrators (reclaiming capacity with confidence).
- The per-project idle-workbench report: what columns mean (last activity,
  owner, reserved resources) and that activity data comes from the notebook
  controller's activity tracking.
- The stale pipeline-run report: the configurable age threshold, how to
  change it, and how retained artifacts are shown.
- Exporting either report as CSV and working with the exported data.
- Safe reclamation steps: what an administrator should verify before stopping
  or removing an idle workbench or deleting a stale run and its artifacts,
  including cautions about data that is still needed.
- Explicit statement of limitations: the reports are read-only; automated
  reclamation and cost/chargeback are not provided.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation topics covering the reports, their data sources, the
  configurable staleness age, CSV export, and safe reclamation steps are
  published in the RHOAI documentation set.
- Every statement about report contents, configuration, and behavior is
  validated against the shipped implementation and matches it (accuracy
  pass).
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implementation by the
  engineering team that built the reporting capability, and review feedback
  is addressed.
- The documentation states that the reports are read-only and does not
  describe reclamation, deletion, or cost features that do not exist.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — Primary. Documentation explains the reports and safe
  reclamation steps.
